newsitem.title: KENYA: OAU team, urging quick action, plans France visit.
newsitem.headline: OAU team, urging quick action, plans France visit.

text.p: Kenyan Foreign Minister Kalonzo Musyoka, still seeking a rapid response to the crisis in eastern Zaire, said on Tuesday he planned to visit ailing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko in southern France.

Musyoka told reporters he would lead a delegation from the Organisation of African Unity's (OAU's) conflict prevention committee to brief Mobutu on international and OAU efforts to resolve the crisis and urge him to play a full role.
Mobutu is convalescing at his luxury villa in Nice after treatment in Switzerland for prostate cancer.
Musyoka said he did not have a departure date, but said his mission would leave as soon as a formal appointment with Mobutu was confirmed.

The OAU's Committee for Conflict Prevention, Management and Resolution met on Monday in Addis Ababa and said it regretted the U.N. Security Council had not deployed a neutral multinational force as urged by an African summit last week in Nairobi.
African countries are particularly annoyed the Security Council said participants in such a force should pay their own bills.

"What that in effect means is that there may be no, or very few African countries that can participate...when it comes to peacekeeping the U.N. must fulfill its responsibilities to Africa," Musyoka said.
The Nairobi summit called for "the immediate setting up of safe corridors and temporary sanctuaries inside Zaire".
But almost one month after the crisis set off by fighting between Tutsi rebels and the army the world has made little progress toward a united response.

France has pushed hardest for intervention to deliver aid to an estimated 1.2 million refugees, but is deeply distrusted by the Tutsi-dominated government in Rwanda for previously supporting its Hutu foes.

U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali confirmed on Tuesday Canada was prepared to command such a force, but said it would need logistical support from the United States -- accused by France of foot-dragging over the issue.
